report:
### Conclusion
The claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) buildup (hypercapnia) is **false**.

### Evidence Supporting Mask Safety
* **Microscopic Gas Permeability:** Carbon dioxide molecules are tiny ($\approx 0.33\text{ nm}$), making them exponentially smaller than the microscopic pores in cloth and surgical mask materials. Consequently, exhaled $\text{CO}_2$ easily passes directly through the mask fabric and around its edges.
* **Clinical Findings:** Research evaluated gas exchange in both healthy adults and individuals with severe respiratory conditions, such as Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD). The study demonstrated that wearing a surgical mask did not produce clinically significant changes in end-tidal $\text{CO}_2$ or oxygen saturation levels.
* **Public Health Consensus:** Medical organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), confirm that properly worn medical and cloth masks do not lead to $\text{CO}_2$ intoxication or oxygen deficiency.
* **Occupational Precedent:** Healthcare professionals routinely wear surgical face masks for prolonged shifts and long surgical procedures without experiencing hypercapnia or oxygen deprivation.

### Sources
* World Health Organization: https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters
* Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/article/fact-check/covid-19-face-masks-do-not-trap-dangerous-levels-of-carbon-dioxide-idUSL1N2T01U3/
* Michigan Medicine: https://www.michiganmedicine.org/health-lab/4-mask-myths-put-you-risk
* Newswise (American Thoracic Society Study): https://www.newswise.com/coronavirus/face-masks-unlikely-to-cause-over-exposure-to-carbon-dioxide-even-in-patients-with-lung-disease
